input.description: Review authentication feature implementation in PR #42. Check for security vulnerabilities, code quality, and test coverage.

output.conclusion: Code review completed with 2 security issues and 1 quality improvement identified. JWT secret is hardcoded (high risk), password validation is weak (medium risk), and error messages expose too much information (low risk).

evidence.description: JWT secret hardcoded in source code

evidence.snippet: if (password.length() < 6) { throw new ValidationException("Password too short"); }

evidence.description: Exception messages returned to client may expose sensitive info

risk.description: Hardcoded JWT secret can be extracted from JAR file, allowing token forgery
risk.mitigation: Move secret to environment variable or secrets manager

risk.description: Weak password validation allows easily guessable passwords
risk.mitigation: Add complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special chars)

risk.description: Error messages may expose internal implementation details
risk.mitigation: Use generic error messages for client, log detailed errors server-side

next_steps.action: Move JWT secret to environment variable (.env file)
Implement strong password validation with complexity requirements
Replace detailed error messages with generic responses
Add security tests for auth bypass attempts
